facts.statement: An incontestable clause bars only contests of validity. It does not stop the insurer from relying at any time on exclusions or restrictions in the policy.
facts.quote: shall not preclude the assertion at any time of defenses based upon provisions in the policy which exclude or restrict coverage

items.stem: A life policy excludes death while piloting a private aircraft. Five years after issue, the insured dies piloting his own plane. Under New Jersey law, the insurer may:
options: Not deny, since the policy is now incontestable
Deny only if the exclusion was in a separate rider
Not deny, since exclusions lapse after 2 years
Deny the claim under the aviation exclusion
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-16 provides that an incontestable clause bars only contests of the policy's validity. The insurer may still rely at any time on policy provisions that exclude or restrict coverage.

facts.statement: A reinstated policy may carry the same exclusions or restrictions that could have applied at original issue, effective from reinstatement.
facts.quote: such reinstated policy may exclude or restrict liability to the same extent that such liability could have been excluded or restricted when the policy was originally issued

items.stem: When a New Jersey life policy is reinstated, the insurer may add an exclusion only if:
options: It was allowable at the policy's original issue
The policyowner agrees to pay a higher premium
The commissioner approves it in advance
It applies only to the first year after reinstatement
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-17 allows a reinstated policy to exclude or restrict liability to the same extent as could have been done at original issue, effective from the reinstatement date.

facts.statement: Under a typical suicide clause, if the insured dies by suicide within the first two years, the insurer pays back the premiums instead of the death benefit.
facts.quote: The insurance company must return premiums paid on the policy.

items.stem: An insured dies by suicide 14 months after a $300,000 policy was issued. The policy has a standard two-year suicide clause. The beneficiary will most likely receive:
options: A sum equal to what the owner paid in
The full $300,000 death benefit
Nothing at all
Half of the death benefit
items.explanation: Per Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations and NC DOI, Standard Policy Provisions and Optional Riders, a suicide clause lets the insurer refuse the death claim for a suicide within the first two years, but the insurer must return the premiums paid.

facts.statement: After the suicide exclusion period ends, death by suicide is covered like any other death.
facts.quote: if a insured commits suicide within the first two years of the insurance contract, the death benefit is limited to the total premiums paid

items.stem: An insured dies by suicide three years after his policy was issued. The policy has a standard two-year suicide clause and has stayed in force. The insurer will:
options: Return the premiums paid instead of the face amount
Pay the full death benefit
Deny the claim, since suicide is a permanent exclusion
Pay the face amount less three years of premiums
items.explanation: Per NC DOI, Standard Policy Provisions and Optional Riders, the suicide clause limits the benefit to premiums paid only for a suicide within the first two years. After that period, the full death benefit is payable.

facts.statement: The incontestable and suicide periods start on the earliest of the date of issue, the policy date and any other effective date (except backdating to save age).
facts.quote: The periods for incontestability and suicide shall commence upon the earliest of the date of issue, the policy date and any other effective date.

items.stem: A New Jersey policy shows a policy date of March 1 and an issue date of March 20, with no backdating to save age. When do the incontestable and suicide periods begin?
options: March 20, the issue date
The date the policy is delivered
March 1, the earlier of the two dates
The date the first premium is paid
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-41.3(b) starts the incontestability and suicide periods on the earliest of the date of issue, the policy date and any other effective date, except when backdating saves age.

facts.statement: When coverage is increased based on new evidence of insurability, the insurer may contest for up to two more years, limited to the increase.
facts.quote: the insurer may reserve a right to contest the policy for no more than an additional two years following the date of the purchase of the increase, but only limited to the actual increase in insurance

items.stem: Five years after issue, a policyowner raises his face amount from $250,000 to $400,000 after a new medical exam. The policy form reserves the insurer's right to contest such increases. Under New Jersey rules, what may the insurer contest?
options: The full $400,000 for two years from the increase
Nothing, since the original policy is past its contestable period
The $250,000 original amount, for one more year
The $150,000 increase, for up to two years from the increase
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-41.3(b) lets the insurer reserve a right to contest for no more than two additional years after an increase bought with new evidence of insurability, limited to the actual increase.

facts.statement: Modifications made without new evidence of insurability, such as cost-of-living or corridor increases, carry no new right to contest.
facts.quote: Insurers shall not retain any right of contest when modifications to the policy occur without additional evidence of insurability, such as corridor or cost of living increases.

items.stem: A policy's cost-of-living rider automatically raises the face amount, with no new application or medical evidence. Under New Jersey rules, the increase:
options: Is not contestable at all
Starts a new two-year contestable period on the increase
Is contestable for one year from the increase
Is contestable until the next policy anniversary
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-41.3(b) bars insurers from retaining any right to contest modifications made without additional evidence of insurability, such as corridor or cost-of-living increases.

facts.statement: On a conversion or change of plan with no increase in the amount at risk, the suicide period under the new policy runs from the original policy's issue date.
facts.quote: the period for death by suicide under the new policy shall begin as of the date of issue of the original policy

items.stem: A term policy issued 18 months ago is converted, at the same face amount and with no increase in the amount at risk, to whole life. The insured dies by suicide 8 months after the conversion. Under New Jersey rules:
options: The suicide exclusion applies, since the whole life policy is only 8 months old
The suicide exclusion does not apply, since the period began with the original policy
The insurer returns premiums paid on the whole life policy only
The claim is contestable for misstatements in the conversion
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-41.3(b) starts the suicide period under the new policy on the original policy's issue date when a conversion does not increase the amount at risk. Here 26 months have passed, so the two-year period has ended.
